reviews.review:
I got this game from a friend and it was a blast.

Short review:
-cons: it's rather short, and Nemeroth sucks
-pros: everything else, especially Warboss Grimskull

Longer review:
The graphics and general atmosphere are spot on for a 40k FPS, with the terrain ranging from claustrophobic sewage pipes, cramped prefabricated buildings, and tight corridor trenches, and deadly factory interiors, to more open platforms, like landing pads, winding slopes, but things are never just too open.  Weapons range from the humble Bolter (a rocket-propelled grenade machine gun wielded as an assault rifle, or a gyrojet that took 3 different steroids and sure as the Emperor did not skip legday), a bolter sniper rifle, plasma guns, to even heavier fare including a portable lasercannon, and my personal favourite: the Jumppack+Thunderhammer combo.
The protagonist Titus comes across as the sheer badass that a Space Marine Captain is supposed to be, but make no mistake: in the 41st Millenium, everything can and WILL kill you even if you're a bio-cybernetically enhanced super soldier in power armour. Be wary at ALL times, do take cover when you have to, and wittle enemies down with guns to a managable amount before destroying them in glorious melee to regain health with execution moves. Remember: there are no health packs, the enemies ARE the health packs!
The gothicy bombastic soundtrack is awesome and fits the mood of nearly constant frantic action, interspliced with short cutscenes that explain the development of the overall situation. Enemies are varied and fun to fight, ranging from the small but most numerous Gretchin to various Orks with different melee berserkers and heavy fire-power-wielding types alike (REALLY watch for the ones with missiles on the higher difficulties), and eventually less numerous but no less deadly renegade soldiers, Chaos Space Marines of various types, and even demonhosts who WILL fry you if you don't take them out quickly enough.
There are two boss battles, one awesome, the other a glorified QTE sequence. Grimskull, the former, is a great boss with lots of character and his defining trait is probably that he just keeps coming back. He's smart, knows when to retreat (highly unusual for an Ork), sets traps, uses enemy equipment, and is all around full of surprises. Taking him down can be very difficult. Nemeroth though... isn't. As stated, he's a glorified QTE, and after having had trouble taking down his 4 waves of reinforcements coming from inside his plot armour forcefield, Titus tackles him and then beats the crap out of him, something I did on the first try with pretty much no effort. So yeah, a waste of a final boss.

So, would I recommend this game? YES, it would definitely get the Emperor's Seal of Approval. It certainly gets mine at least.

This is still a very solid game in 2019. I just finished the campaign on Hard and it was a good 12 hours of fun.

Power Armor feels like an actual Power Armor in this game. It has momentum when you run and impact-sounds are very good.

Almost all the weapons feel and sound powerful. Very much 40K. Melee takes a bit of getting used to, since swings have momentum and you can't interrupt animations. But when you get the hang of it, it feels really good.

The main campaign is solid and the story is what you would expect form WH40K: interesting and very macho. Voice acting is pretty good and environments somewhat varied. You get upgrades to your weapons and gear along the way.

The game has aged surprisingly well graphically. Ultrawide resolution works, although the FOV could be a bit bigger.

Nobody plays multiplayer anymore, so expect campaign only. There is a coop horde-mode, if you have friends.

Buy on sale.
